newsitem.title: USA: Honda says CR-V to boost 1997 U.S. sales.
newsitem.headline: Honda says CR-V to boost 1997 U.S. sales.

text.p: Honda Motor Co Ltd said on Wednesday it expects to boost its U.S. vehicle sales to another record in 1997, thanks in part to increased production of the new CR-V small sport/utility vehicle.

Richard Colliver, senior vice president of sales for American Honda Motor Co, said the automaker now expects to sell about 60,000 CR-Vs annually, about twice as many as it projected earlier this year.
Speaking to reporters at a news briefing here, Colliver said Honda has started a second production line at its plant in Sayama, Japan, to keep up with CR-V demand.

The sport/utility is based on the automaker's Civic small car platform and is expected to sell for less than $20,000 for a fully-equipped, four-wheel-drive model. It will compete with Toyota Motor Corp.'s RAV4 and will arrive in showrooms starting in January.

Colliver said Honda now expects to sell about 775,000 vehicles in the United States during 1997, compared to about 730,000 expected for 1996. The 1996 total, up from 697,228 units in 1995, will break Honda's previous U.S. sales record, set in 1990.
Honda also expects a smaller boost from the introduction of a redesigned 1997 Prelude sport coupe. Colliver said Honda expects to sell 20,000 Preludes next year, compared to about 12,000 this year.

The sporty car will start at around $23,000 -- about the same price as last year -- but will offer more standard features. Honda's more powerful VTEC engine will be standard equipment on all 1997 Preludes.
"It's the same price, but there's a lot more value to it," Colliver said.
